title: Creamy Tomato Chicken Penne
summary: Golden pan-seared chicken simmered in a rich tomato and cream sauce, tossed with penne and wilted spinach for an easy midweek pasta.
equipment: large, deep frying pan or sauté pan (30 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: fine salt, for the pasta water
skinless chicken breast, cut into 2.5 cm pieces

ingredients.note: plus extra to serve if you like (not counted)

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Season the chicken with the 1/4 teaspoon salt, then heat the oil in the 30 cm deep pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and brown for 4-5 minutes, turning once, until golden on two sides — it doesn't need to be cooked through yet, since it finishes later in the sauce. Lift onto a plate and set aside.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add the onion to the same pan over medium heat and cook for 6-8 minutes until soft and translucent, scraping up the browned bits stuck to the base as you go. That fond holds concentrated flavour from the chicken and feeds straight into the sauce. Stir in the garlic, oregano and chilli flakes for 1 minute.

steps.title: Deepen the tomato purée
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée and fry it for 1-2 minutes until it darkens to a brick-red colour. This brief cooking caramelises the purée's natural sugars, softening its raw, tinny edge into something deeper and sweeter.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the chopped tomatoes along with 100 ml water used to rinse out the tin, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Meanwhile, boil the penne in salted water for 1 minute less than the packet time, then save 150 ml of the pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Finish the chicken
steps.text: Return the chicken and its juices to the sauce and simmer gently for 4-5 minutes, until the largest piece reaches 74°C in the centre with no pink remaining. Lower the heat, stir in the cream, then take the pan off the boil before stirring in the cheese — adding it while the sauce bubbles hard can make it turn grainy. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Add the drained pasta to the pan with a splash of the reserved pasta water, tossing until glossy and the sauce coats every tube. Taste and adjust the salt, then scatter the basil over the top before serving.

tips: Don't let the sauce boil hard once the cream and cheese go in — a gentle simmer keeps it smooth instead of grainy or split.
If your pan is on the smaller side, brown the chicken in two batches rather than crowding it, so it colours instead of steaming.
Double cream holds up well to simmering; a lighter single cream is more prone to splitting, so stick with double for a reliably silky sauce.
Leftover sauce thickens as it sits in the fridge — loosen it with a splash of water as you reheat.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water, or in the microwave stirring occasionally, until piping hot throughout (74°C). The sauce alone freezes well for up to 2 months — just add freshly cooked pasta after thawing.
